name: Buffer
tagline: Social media scheduler for publishing posts across channels

pricing.notes: Official pricing/help checked 2026-07-30; Essentials listed at $6/channel/month monthly and $5/channel/month annually.

verdictSummary: Posting to one or two APIs is easy, but maintaining social platform auth, queues, previews, analytics, and API-policy compliance is real ongoing work.
coreLoopDIY: Create a post queue, connect one social API, schedule jobs, publish posts, and log outcomes.
requirements: OAuth/API access for each social network
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because social APIs break and scheduling must be reliable.

priorArt.name: Postiz
priorArt.desc: Open-source social media scheduling tool and strong Buffer-like prior art.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: Six networks, a visual editor and a thousand scheduled posts a month; analytics and team workflow are not invited.

alternatives.name: BrightBean Studio
alternatives.desc: A startlingly complete free scheduler: approvals, inbox, analytics, clients, API and MCP, with someone else running the servers.

alternatives.name: Buffer Free
alternatives.desc: Three channels, ten queued posts each and thirty days of metrics; eight lifetime channel connections make swapping a one-way door.

alternatives.name: Fedica Free
alternatives.desc: Ten network accounts and ten queued posts total, refilling forever; generous until you plan eleven things at once.

alternatives.name: Mixpost Lite
alternatives.desc: A polished single-user scheduler with queues and basic analytics; the serious team features live in the paid edition.

alternatives.name: Postiz
alternatives.desc: The broadest open scheduler here; free means running PostgreSQL, Redis, Temporal and your own platform credentials.

alternatives.name: Publer Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts and ten queued posts each; yesterday's history disappears tomorrow.

alternatives.name: Social Champ Free
alternatives.desc: Three non-X accounts, fifteen queued posts each, analytics and an inbox; one user and no X publishing.

notes: Great social example: one channel is easy; social-platform maintenance is not.
prompt:
Build me a personal social post scheduler to replace Buffer. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3; a localhost page with a compose box,
  image attach, and the queue ordered by send time.
- Two targets only: Mastodon (access token) and Bluesky (app password via
  @atproto/api), creds in .env. One small adapter file per network so a
  third is addable later, but scaffold nothing I don't use.
- Buffer-style slots: I define posting times (say weekdays 09:00 and 17:00
  in my timezone) and new posts fill the next free slot; a post can also be
  pinned to an exact datetime.
- A node-cron tick every minute publishes due posts, marks each row sent or
  failed, retries failures 3 times with backoff, and marks before sending so
  nothing ever double-posts.
- Per-network character counter in the composer; attached images stored in
  media/ next to the database.
- A history page of the last 100 sent posts linking to the live posts.
- Runs on my always-on box; localhost only, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Out of scope: X, Instagram, and LinkedIn (paid, approval-gated, or hostile
  APIs, say so in the README), analytics, and rich post previews.
- README: getting a Mastodon access token and a Bluesky app password.
